video_title: Calvin Johnson Targeted Patrick Peterson 22 TIMES in Their First Matchup

quotes.speaker: Brice Butler
quotes.summary_phrase: Brice Butler on the mental demands of guarding elite receivers
quotes.excerpt: You have to watch his every single move.
quotes.quote: If you are having to guard a guy and be with a guy everywhere that he goes on the field, you have to watch his every single move. For an example, when I had the opportunity to go up against Calvin Johnson, it was my first time going up against him, my second year in the league. I felt I had a pretty good game, but watching film on him, I have to know what he is doing when he is in the slot, when he is the X, when he is the Z, when he motion, when he is off the ball. You have to watch all of these things versus when you are in a system, you are just doing your job.

quotes.speaker: Brice Butler
quotes.summary_phrase: Brice Butler on being targeted 22 times by Calvin Johnson
quotes.excerpt: I got targeted 22 times. He caught 10.
quotes.quote: My first time going up against Calvin Johnson, I got targeted 22 times. He caught 10. I had a pick. I think I had three PBU's. So like I said, I thought it was a pretty solid game. That's a solid game. 22 targets, less than 50 percent. I went to work. That's probably your highest activity you ever had in your career, bro.

quotes.speaker: Brice Butler
quotes.summary_phrase: Brice Butler on the rarity of route concepts in the NFL
quotes.excerpt: You never saw the rub route at the NFL level for the most part.
quotes.quote: I think me and Darrell Revis, I'm a firm believer in this, you never saw the rub route at the NFL level for the most part. You never really saw receiver screens for the most part in the NFL level. Darrell Revis had to be the most receiver screen, pick player DB in the game, by far. Yeah. Someone else is they are trying to get in your way to make a play because they know their best player is going to be on you all game and we need him to at least try to make a play.

quotes.speaker: Brice Butler
quotes.summary_phrase: Brice Butler on Eli Manning's hand signals
quotes.excerpt: I was taunting Eli Manning because he used the same hand signals as Eli Manning.
quotes.quote: We were playing the New York Giants, I can't remember the year, but I was taunting Eli Manning because he used the same hand signals as Eli Manning. And he did something on his hip or did something like this and the receiver ran a go. So I ran the route for him and the quarterback threw the ball out of bounds. And Eli Manning happened to be there. I said, Eli, man, tell him to change up the signal, man. I watched tape, man. I already knew that was going over.

quotes.speaker: Brice Butler
quotes.summary_phrase: Brice Butler on his worst NFL game against Julio Jones
quotes.excerpt: Julio Jones gave me my worst game of my career.
quotes.quote: I never forget this game. 2014, we traveled down to Atlanta. We played Julio Jones, you know Matt Ryan. Was Roddy White still there? Yeah, Roddy was there. They were rolling at the time. And Julio Jones gave me my worst game of my career. Julio dropped, I think 192. And it was just off straight comebacks. Literally ran, he caught nine 18-yard comebacks the entire game. And then just turned them up. It was like, he was making great catches just out of bounds. Some of them may have been longer than 18 yards, but they were all comebacks on the sideline for the most part.

quotes.speaker: Brice Butler
quotes.summary_phrase: Brice Butler on his 2015 All-Pro season
quotes.excerpt: I had an All-Pro year, made my fifth Pro Bowl that year.
quotes.quote: Came back, had an All-Pro year, made my fifth Pro Bowl that year. We lost NFC Championship that year, but that year, I think I gave up one touchdown, had two interceptions. My completion rate against me that year was like 23. So it was something crazy, but having the opportunity to really dig down deep and find it, find that again and have that fight and knowing who you are, that's where to me the short memory came from.
